newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japanese Emperor Akihito meets Brazil's Cardoso.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Emperor Akihito meets Brazil's Cardoso.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko met Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in a formal ceremony on Monday, the second full day of their two-week official visit to South America.

In a blaze of pomp and high security, the imperial couple was welcomed by Cardoso and Brazilian first lady Ruth Cardoso in front of the presidential palace in Brasilia as cannons fired off a salvo of ceremonial shots nearby.

The emperor and the president spent just more than an hour talking about a range of subjects such as the cultural ties between Japan and Brazil, a spokesman for Cardoso said. About 1.3 million people of Japanese descent live in Brazil, the largest overseas Japanese community.
"The president was very pleased to receive the emperor and said he will find few countries enjoy the kind of friendship and culture similarities as Brazil and Japan," the spokesman said.

The emperor said he was interested in a book written by Ruth Cardoso on Brazil's Japanese community, while the president expressed his satisfaction at the levels of Japanese investment flowing into Brazil, the spokesman added.
Others who attended the meeting said the emperor also talked about the carp swimming in a palace pond and praised Brazilian music. Akihito has published several books on fish.

During the meeting the palace was ringed by Brazilian and Japanese security officials. In a break with tradition, Japanese police were accompanying the royal couple, who are normally protected by imperial guards.

The switch was seen in Japan as a sign of heightened security concerns in the wake of the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru, by left-wing guerrillas in December and the subsequent four-month siege.
Akihito is the first Japanese emperor to visit South America. He arrived on Saturday and on Sunday went for a boat ride near the mouth of the Amazon River.

The emperor and empress were due to attend an official dinner later on Monday before touring Brasilia's futuristic centre on Tuesday. Later in the week they travel to Belo Horizonte, Sao Paulo, Curitiba and Rio de Janeiro before flying to Buenos Aires on June 9 for a three-day visit to Argentina.
